from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
from pathlib import Path

input_path = Path('/mnt/data/spreadsheet/44264/1_44264_input.xlsx')
output_path = Path('/mnt/data/outputs/44264_0_c362ae6f/1_44264_output.xlsx')
output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

wb = load_workbook(input_path)
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Dynamic, backward-compatible rolling 3-week percentage formula:
# - the data range expands/shrinks automatically down columns G:H
# - row criterion is taken from I7:I9
# - column week is taken from J5:N5
# - the 3-week slot is [week, week+3), i.e. week, week+1, week+2
#
# Formula uses INDEX/LOOKUP + COUNTIFS/COUNTIF rather than newer dynamic-array
# functions so it works in older Excel versions as well.
last_row_expr = 'LOOKUP(2,1/($H:$H<>""),ROW($H:$H))'
qty_rng = f'$G$6:INDEX($G:$G,{last_row_expr})'
week_rng = f'$H$6:INDEX($H:$H,{last_row_expr})'

for row in range(7, 10):
    for col in range(10, 15):  # J:N
        col_letter = get_column_letter(col)
        formula = (
            f'=IFERROR('
            f'COUNTIFS({qty_rng},$I{row},{week_rng},">="&{col_letter}$5,{week_rng},"<"&{col_letter}$5+3)'
            f'/COUNTIF({qty_rng},$I{row}),'
            f'0)'
        )
        cell = ws.cell(row=row, column=col)
        cell.value = formula
        cell.number_format = '0.00%'

# Encourage recalculation when opened in Excel/LibreOffice.
try:
    wb.calculation.fullCalcOnLoad = True
    wb.calculation.forceFullCalc = True
    wb.calculation.calcMode = "auto"
except Exception:
    pass

wb.save(output_path)
print(f"Saved to {output_path}")
for r in range(7, 10):
    print([ws.cell(r, c).value for c in range(10, 15)])
